subject: Urgent: spike in p95/p99 latency after GPU pool thaw - FinSecure
messages:
From: Tom Bradley <tom@finsecure.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 1 Aug 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Hosted API — morning p99 spike after scale-up

Kimberly,

This morning (08:45–09:05 PDT) we saw sustained p95/p99 latency spikes on the hosted endpoint powering our payments flow. Rough symptoms: 504s for short requests, token-level latency jumping to 6–12s at p99, and a 30% drop in throughput during the window. Our telemetry shows these correlate with a pool thaw event (autoscale from standby to warm) in your us-west pool.

I’m attaching the trace IDs we could capture (trace-snapshot.json) and a few request timestamps. Can you confirm if anything changed on your side? This is causing user-impact and we need an ETA on mitigation + a short-term workaround.

Thanks,
Tom
Ops Lead, FinSecure
[attachment: trace-snapshot.json (application/json)]
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
To: Tom Bradley <tom@finsecure.com>
Cc: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 1 Aug 2027 09:34:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Hosted API — morning p99 spike after scale-up

Tom — thanks for the heads up and the traces. Sorry for the disruption.

Immediate steps we’re taking:
- I’ve looped in SRE (Sean) and infra eng (Vivek) to triage live telemetry.
- We will pause non-critical autoscale events for your account for the next 2 hours while we investigate.
- Can you confirm the top 3 request IDs and any long prompt examples? That’ll speed up matching on our side.

Short-term mitigations we can apply with your sign-off:
1) Increase warm instance retention for your pool from 30s -> 300s to reduce thaw frequency.
2) Apply a temporary per-route soft-rate-limit and fallback to a smaller model (same API) for tail requests.

We’ll aim to have a mitigation plan in the next 45 minutes and a rollback plan documented.

–Kimberly
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
Redwood Inference | kimberly_park@redwood.ai
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, Tom Bradley <tom@finsecure.com>
Cc: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 1 Aug 2027 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Hosted API — morning p99 spike after scale-up

On Sun, Aug 1, 2027 at 9:34 AM Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Tom — thanks for the heads up and the traces. Sorry for the disruption.

Quick notes from an infra perspective after a first pass of the trace:
- The traces show a ~7–9s stall between container start and first token emission for a subset of requests routed to the standby-to-warm path. That aligns with our expected kernel load + KV cache fill for large-context models but is higher than our typical median (we normally see ~2–3s).
- A recent change in pool scheduling (opt-in to lower memory consolidation) can increase cold-to-warm startup for certain instance types; we rolled that to a subset of hosts last week for cost reasons.

Proposed engineering mitigations (fast path):
- Temporarily revert the consolidation policy for your dedicated pool (5–10 minute ops change) — requires your permission to apply to your pool only.
- Pre-warm common KV cache prefixes for your top routes (we can use the request samples you provided) — non-disruptive, can be tested in canary.

Longer term: we’ll add a standby-to-warm SLA and improve prefetch heuristics.

I’ll coordinate the revert + pre-warm if you approve. Will also post the exact rollback steps in the playbook.

Vivek
Senior Engineering Manager, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference
From: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>
To: Tom Bradley <tom@finsecure.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 1 Aug 2027 10:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Hosted API — morning p99 spike after scale-up

Tom / Kimberly —

We have a short mitigation playbook ready:
- Apply pool-specific revert of memory consolidation flag (targeted, non-global). Estimated rollout 2–4 minutes, monitored with rolling canary.
- Increase warm retention for the affected pool to 300s.
- Enable KV prefix pre-warm for the top 5 routes (we will use your traces to seed).

If you approve, we’ll run the canary on one host and monitor p95/p99 for 15 minutes before rolling to the rest. Links:
- Live pool dashboard: https://console.redwood.ai/dashboards/finsecure/pools/27
- Playbook: [attachment: warmup-playbook.pdf (application/pdf)]

Please confirm and we’ll proceed.

—Sean
Principal SRE, Redwood Inference
From: Tom Bradley <tom@finsecure.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>
Cc: Laura Chen <laura.chen@finsecure.com>, procurement@finsecure.com
Date: Sun, 1 Aug 2027 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Hosted API — morning p99 spike after scale-up

Kimberly / Sean — thanks for the rapid response. Please proceed with the targeted revert + pre-warm canary. We approve the change to warm retention.

Two asks from us:
1) Please share the expected timeline for the full rollout and confirmation once p99 is back within our baseline.
2) Given customer impact, we’d like a goodwill credit for the affected time window and a short exec briefing for our CTO (looping Laura).

We’ll send any additional traces we find. Appreciate the quick coordination.

Tom
Ops Lead, FinSecure
